title: Per-layer quant routing and accuracy validation pipeline for mixed-precision inference
creator: Sofia Hernandez
description: Implement a per-layer quant-routing and accuracy validation pipeline that allows the runtime to select between FP16 / FP8 / INT8 kernel paths dynamically. This ticket covers: collection of per-layer calibration histograms, a calibration job that emits quantization profiles with per-op error budgets, offline accuracy validation harness against a golden prompt set, and a runtime kernel selector that uses latency/accuracy policies to dispatch mixed-precision paths. The goal is safe automated down-precision (FP8/INT8) where quality is preserved within operator-level budgets and overall model-level thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration job collects per-layer activation distributions and emits stable quant profiles (json blob) for FP8 and INT8 with metadata tags for sequence length and batch shape.

Offline validation harness runs 10k prompt set and reports end-to-end metric drift (perplexity / EM / Rouge as applicable) and per-layer contribution; allowed model-level drift <= 0.75% for P0 models.
Runtime kernel selector accepts a quant profile and per-request accuracy budget and dispatches per-layer kernels (FP16/FP8/INT8) deterministically with a fallback path to FP16 on mismatches.
End-to-end performance test shows >20% token-cost reduction for quantized path on targeted models with median p50 latency delta < 10ms compared to FP16 baseline under target batch sizes.
Console rollout UI surfaces quant-profile version, observed drift, and can flag and rollback policy when accuracy thresholds are exceeded.
Unit/integration tests added for profile ingestion, selector logic, and fallback correctness; CI passes on GPU and CPU emulation where applicable.
implementation_steps: Design: finalize quant-profile schema (per-op histograms, scale/zero metadata, calibrator seed info, supported sequence length buckets). See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Per-Layer+Quant+Schema
Calibration job: extend offline calibration worker to collect activation histograms by op and layer; support reservoir sampling for long-tail tokens.
Profile generator: implement heuristics to compute per-op quant buckets and an 'error budget' score that estimates output drift contribution.
Validation harness: build evaluation runner that computes model-level metrics across golden prompt set and produces a validation report (CSV + JSON).
Runtime selector: add a kernel dispatch module that accepts profile + request budget and emits per-layer kernel targets and fallback pointers.
Rollout controls: wire selector telemetry to Console for rollout gating and add API to pin profile versions to deployments.
Testing: stress E2E under target throughput, add unit tests for histogram ingestion, and run A/B on a canary host group.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive per-op quantization yields cost wins but increases risk of localized accuracy regressions. We will use per-op error budgets and a conservative default policy for canary rollouts.
We decided against a single global scale per-tensor approach; per-layer profiles preserve quality for large attention matrices while allowing smaller MLP layers to go lower-precision.

Calibration sampling: reservoir sampling protects tail distributions on long context tasks. Recording full activation distributions for production models is too heavy; we summarize with histograms and percentile sketches.

Kernel selection policy combines three signals: estimated token-cost savings, per-op estimated drift, and measured runtime latency profile for the target hardware. A weighted scoring function is used (configurable in runtime).
Fallbacks: runtime must be able to atomically fall back a layer to FP16 if execution raises numerical exceptions or observed output drift exceeds thresholds mid-rollout.
